correctness.rationale: Forward positivity is explicit and witnessed on a nonempty open invariant region. The subcritical prey quotient has a convergent positive product; the predator law follows from an absolutely convergent product of normalized prey terms. At the critical multiplier, predation is smaller than every prey power, so reciprocal prey increments give 1+1/(2u)+O(u^-2); a convergent shift and Gamma-normalized product give the precise stretched-lognormal coefficient. Independent numerical runs check examples but not infinity.

value.rationale: The paper leaves the neutral zero-population boundary outside its global stability theorem. The precise transition from quadratic-in-generation predator log decay to factorial decay with a universal -(log n)^2/4 correction is a natural, nontrivial quantitative law that cannot be replaced by knowing the neutral multiplier or the leading prey 1/n law. It sharpens the expected detection and eradication clocks of the same model while maintaining its viability restriction.
